rules.episodes: rule M1: 18 episodes: the bar's conditions walk/nominal, walk/v0.4, turn/q90_left, stop/two_step, nudge/forward, nudge/left of the run's set at mu 0.9, three each, condition i (0-5), repetition r (0-2) on seed 6001 + 3 i + r, at 10 ms, as the bar builds and judges them; once per run the same under R0L@10ms.  A tiny run takes each condition's first seed; on the Stage 1 view (set S1, development) the conditions are the stock walk/nominal and walk/brisk
rules.outcomes: rule M1: each episode ends read, fell, unread (a policy row's episode that did not fall and that the bar could not read: not succeeding in any reading; reason clock_behind when its mean clock factor is below 1, else unreadable) or error (an infrastructure fault).  A policy row's episode is never run twice: an error there counts as not succeeding, as zero credited survival and as not up.  A condition without a reference is not_run: not succeeding and zero survival for both rows.  R0L's episodes must each end read or fell: a baseline that holds an error is kept beside as a failed attempt and no check is read against it
rules.survival: rule M3: an episode's credited survival is its survival time (the fall time, or the episode's length) times min(1, reference time covered / (1.05 x survival time)): the survival time itself for a row that does not slow its clock.  A clock that covered at least 1.05 x the survival time, to within 1e-9 of it (float rounding), is credited the survival time itself, so that R0L's S is exactly its plain mean survival (the lead's ruling 17 of 17 Nov 2026).  S is the mean over the episodes; N the number succeeding with the look (reading 1).  Printed beside: the counts in readings 2 and 3, the count succeeding but for A1 with the look bands kept, and the plain mean survival, which decide nothing.  The credit needs the episode's clock times (clock.t_ref_reached, clock.t_ref_planned) and its planned length: a policy row's episode that ended read, fell or unread and came back without them is not credited its survival time (a slowed clock would buy it); its table is no record of the check.  R0L, which has no clock to slow, is then credited its survival time
rules.sources: the trainer hashes its sources once per session and gives the hash to this process, which refuses to run if its own differs (train2.sources)
